title: Add three operations to an expression tree

task.text: Expressions are a stable tree; the operations over it keep growing.
Finish the **Visitor** over `Expr` (`Num`, `Add`, `Mul`, `Neg`). `ExprVisitor<R>` is given and must not change.

items: Each node's `accept(ExprVisitor<R>)` calls the visit method for its own type and returns its result.
`Show` returns fully parenthesised text: `((2 + 3) * 4)`, `-(5)`, a lone number as `9`.
`Depth` returns 1 for a number, otherwise 1 plus its deepest child.
Operations reach children only through `accept(this)`: no `instanceof`, no `switch`, and no operation named in a node class.

checks.title: Each node calls its own visit method

hints.text: Double dispatch: the node knows its own type, the visitor knows the operation. Each `accept` hands `this` to the visit method that matches the node. That is the only thing a node does.
Write `accept` as a single return in every record. In the operations, evaluate a child with `child.accept(this)` and combine the results; the visitor's result type `R` carries the answer.
